title: TT-Bio: biomolecular structure, design and embeddings on Tenstorrent
subtitle: Five structure-prediction models at 512 residues, measured on Tenstorrent Blackhole and on NVIDIA H200, B200 and A100.
notes: This file is the only place numbers are edited. index.html reads it and derives everything else.
Never write a derived value here. Server throughput, cost per hour and both throughput-per-dollar charts are computed in the page from s_per_fold, accelerators, price and power.

One cell per model per platform, holding the fastest measured arm that passes parity against its own reference. Every Tenstorrent cell states which parity it holds: bit-exact, byte-identical, or a measured structural delta inside a bar that was fixed before the number existed. A cell with no measurement gets status 'blocked' and a reason. Do not fill it with an estimate.

The A100 is a card-only column: it carries no cost figure, because no DGX A100 price and power are sourced here. It appears in the per-card charts and tables and in neither throughput-per-dollar chart.

scope.description: CDK2 (PDB 1HCL) tandem-duplicated to 512 residues, one protein chain, no ligands, a fixed 35-sequence MSA.
scope.protocol: Warm folds, one prediction at a time on one accelerator, the same two input files on both sides, each model at its own recycle and sampling-step settings. Each Tenstorrent cell is that model's fastest arm that passes parity.

cost_model.amortisation_basis: Four years is this page's assumption for how long an AI accelerator earns its keep: one year shorter than the general-purpose server life Amazon reports in its 10-Q, because an accelerator generation lasts about two years. A shorter window favours the cheaper box, so the range below brackets it.
cost_model.utilisation: The machine predicts continuously, so every hour of ownership is an hour of throughput.
cost_model.formula: Throughput per dollar, with the DGX H200 set to 1.00x, on two bases. Purchase price: predictions per hour / price, with no amortisation window, because the window cancels from that ratio. Total cost of ownership: predictions per hour / cost per hour, where cost per hour = price / (4 x 8766 h) + power kW x $/kWh.
cost_model.sensitivity: Shift the window to 3 or 6 years, or the rate to the 13.54 c/kWh US commercial tariff, and the Tenstorrent figure moves between 2.47x and 3.71x. It does not invert.

p150a.parity: 0.3248 A CA RMSD, inside the 0.35 A bar fixed before the measurement
p150a.ref: Median of three warm folds on one p150a, 82.372 / 82.393 / 82.422 s, spread 0.050 s, measured uninstrumented on the shipped path, cold fold discarded. The 82.942 s this cell carried before is the same measurement without the host-side glue: the relative-position one-hot is now scattered into an fp32 result instead of built from int64 one-hots and an int64 concatenation, and the trunk-to-structural pair copy stays in the bf16 the device already held. Both are bit-exact and both are host time, worth 0.498 s at the fold with the CIF digest unchanged and the device wall flat to inside its own spread. This is the one cell that is not bit-exact against the reference: the triangle-attention matmul folds its contraction in twelve-tile blocks, worth one bf16 unit in the last place, so the CIF digest moves 50aa1e46583bd5a8 to 357c67003bb738ac and plDDT 0.754131 to 0.754110. The structural cost is 0.3248 A Kabsch CA, measured on a monomeric 298-residue control because this fixture's two domains hinge freely and saturate the metric. The byte-identical arm at the same two matmul settings returns 88.61 s.

h200.ref: Median of n=3, spread 0.29 %. opendde 1.0.3, torch 2.7.1+cu128, plDDT 0.827.

b200.detail: The same hang, same signature. OpenDDE pins cuequivariance-ops-torch 0.10.0. The three models that run clean on the B200 all resolve 0.11.1, so the split follows the cuEquivariance version rather than the model.

a100.ref: Median of n=3 warm, 40.220 / 40.151 / 40.167 s, spread 0.17 %, cold 44.020 s discarded. opendde 1.0.3, torch 2.7.1+cu128, cuEquivariance 0.10.0, plDDT 0.823. cueqops_triangle_attention 1216 and cueqops_triangle_multiplicative_update 1216. The version that hangs on B200 runs clean on Ampere.

p150a.ref: Six warm folds of the shipped default, two processes under benchlock on qb2 card 3 (perf/of3_4xpd/xmodel_qb2c3/openfold3_B1.json and _B2.json): 38.199 / 38.212 / 38.247 / 38.261 / 38.329 / 38.351 s, median 38.254, spread 0.152 s. Measured against main in the same alternating run, which folded the same fixture on the same card in 44.541 s median, so the gain is 6.287 s and neither arm inherits a number from another day. Four levers since the 44.535 cell, each measured in its own alternating A/B. The template embedder runs its pair stack once per DISTINCT template slot: a query with no templates fills all four slots from the same dummy precursor, so three of four were the same two blocks on the same values, four times over per recycle. The AdaLN conditioning half is a function of the atom conditioning alone, so its nine layer-norm-plus-two-linear groups are computed once per diffusion rollout instead of once in each of 401 atom-transformer calls. The 512 per-residue reference conformers are embedded on a thread pool, each residue keeping the ETKDG seed the sequential loop would have drawn for it. And TriangleAttention's additive pair bias is cast to fp32 once per call instead of once in each of its 43 row blocks. Bit-exact: CIF sha256 da9b4ed68f8c0405 and plDDT 0.547851 on all twelve warm folds of both arms, the same digest the 44.535 cell carried. The two shared-code levers, the AdaLN split and the fp32 bias hoist, were also A/B'd against Boltz-2, ESMFold2, Protenix-v2 and OpenDDE on this card: same digest and same plDDT in every arm, no perf change outside each model's own spread (perf/of3_4xpd/xmodel_qb2c3/).

h200.ref: Median of n=3, spread 0.21 %. openfold3 0.4.4, torch 2.13.0+cu130, checkpoint of3-p2-155k.pt, plDDT 0.639.

a100.ref: Median of n=3 warm, 16.942 / 16.942 / 16.892 s, spread 0.30 %, cold 22.186 s discarded. openfold3 0.4.4, torch 2.13.0+cu130, ckpt of3-p2-155k.pt, plDDT 0.638. triangle_attention 2752 and triangle_multiplicative_update 1702 through the kernels, every torch-fallback counter 0.

design.deck: BoltzGen and RFdiffusion3, seconds per binder design on one AI Processor, each on its own pinned target.
design.cond: Wall-clock seconds to return one binder design on a single AI Processor, warm, at each model's shipped defaults. Shorter is better. Every platform runs one design at a time, the same protocol as the folding rows above, on the same target with the same settings.
design.note: No throughput-per-dollar figure is derived here. The rung above this one overflows L1 on the p150a for BoltzGen, so BoltzGen is measured one rung below it, where the H200 sits at 41 % of its power limit and the B200 at 31 %, and a cost ratio taken on an idle GPU would not survive a bigger target. On both models the B200 is no faster than the H200: 18.5 % slower on RFdiffusion3 and 1.27x slower on BoltzGen. Asking for eight designs at once instead of one changes only the GPUs. RFdiffusion3 amortises a batch of eight by 2.12x on the H200, 2.50x on the B200 and 1.79x on the A100, so eight designs take 103.79 s on an H200, 104.39 s on a B200, 198.20 s on an A100 and 987.96 s on a p150a; the p150a gains nothing from batching at this target size and runs one design at a time by default. The rows above carry a bit-exact digest; a design draws a new sequence every time, so these two carry per-run output validation instead, and every design counted here wrote, parsed, had finite coordinates and had the residue topology its spec asked for.
design.methods: Two pinned targets, one per model, at the shipped defaults: BoltzGen 500 sampling steps, RFdiffusion3 200 timesteps, one design at a time on both. Tenstorrent figures are warm medians on one Blackhole p150a under a run lock, with the cold pass and, for BoltzGen, the design that pays the checkpoint switch dropped. GPU figures come from the same protocol on rented single-GPU nodes. Designs are validated per run rather than digested: chain sizes, residue topology and finite coordinates, never atom equality between siblings, because sibling designs legitimately differ.

models.name: BoltzGen
models.target: EBV gp350 D123 (9ma0 chain A), 414 target residues, 100-residue binder, 514 tokens

p150a.ref: Median of n=4 warm designs, 45.187 / 45.221 / 45.357 / 45.393 s, spread 0.46 %, with a second independent process 0.05 % away at 45.265 s. qb2, Blackhole p150a physical card 0, ttnn 0.68.0, under a run lock. End-to-end per design; the cold design and the design that pays the 1.9 GB checkpoint switch are dropped, the same two the GPU arm drops. 500 sampling steps resolved from the shipped design.yaml and asserted per design. 20.501 s of each design is the denoising loop at 41.00 ms per step, the other 24.8 s is trunk, post-processing and writing.

h200.ref: Median of n=4 warm designs, spread 1.18 %, end-to-end per design. boltzgen 0.1.0, torch 2.13.0+cu130, fused kernels on. The cold design and the design that pays the checkpoint switch are dropped.

b200.ref: Median of n=4 warm designs, spread 0.59 %, end-to-end per design, same stack.

a100.ref: Median of n=4 warm designs end-to-end, 21.115 s per design plus the 0.614 s median inter-loop gap; per-design spread 1.58 %, and an independent second process 1.7 % away at 21.419 s. boltzgen 0.3.2, torch 2.13.0+cu130, cuEquivariance 0.11.1. Cold design and the design that pays the 1.9 GB checkpoint switch both dropped, the same two every other arm drops. cueq_trimul 3360 and cueq_triatt 3360; 96 of 3456 triangle-attention calls (2.78 %) miss the kernel through the same upstream plumbing gap seen on H200 and B200. Every design parses to 100 designed plus 414 target residues with no non-finite coordinates. Peak 7229 MiB.

models.name: RFdiffusion3
models.target: Human serum albumin (9q6y chain A), 585 target residues, 100-residue binder, 6051 atoms

p150a.ref: Median of n=3 warm forwards, 113.649 / 114.706 / 114.134 s per forward of 1, spread 0.93 %, 570.7 ms per timestep. qb2, Blackhole p150a physical card 0, ttnn 0.68.0, under a run lock. The run asked for the shipped batch of 8; the runtime runs 1 at this target size, because batching stops paying above 2952 atoms — measured at 3844 atoms it is worth 1.04x, under the 1.05x bar to change the default. Two bitwise-identical wins are on by default here: matmul program-config calibration, worth 1.166x, and a tile-aligned pair concat, worth 1.082x. The second one gathers the distogram and self-conditioning one-hots as a single 160-wide table lookup instead of two 65-wide ones, because ttnn.concat runs 15x below its bandwidth floor if any input is narrower than a 32-wide tile: 25.35 ms against 1.68 for the same tensor built from aligned pieces. Four alternating folds, two with the concat change and two without, all wrote CIF sha256 382e7b23ae8cfc75. All four designs of this run wrote 6051 atoms and 685 residues and passed validation.

h200.ref: Median of n=3 warm designs, 27.24 / 27.49 / 28.02 s, spread 2.84 %, one design per forward. rc-foundry 0.2.0 with the current production attention path, torch 2.13.0+cu130, 381.5 W, 54.5 % of the box's own 700 W limit at 79 % utilisation. Ask it for eight designs at once instead and it returns them in 103.79 s, 12.974 s each, at 98 % utilisation and 553.1 W: batching is worth 2.12x to an H200 because one design does not fill it.

b200.ref: Median of n=3 warm designs, spread 1.50 %, one design per forward, same stack. 18.5 % slower than the H200 at one design. At eight at once it returns 13.049 s each, an amortisation of 2.50x.

a100.ref: Median of n=3 warm batches, 43.91 / 44.29 / 44.44 s, spread 1.20 %, cold 45.18 s discarded, batch 1. rc-foundry 0.2.0 plus the 4010e3e2e attention.py, torch 2.13.0+cu130, checkpoint rfd3_latest.ckpt sha256 9b3f8592. dense_sdpa_pairbias_attention 7164, sparse 28656, cuEquivariance unreachable by code so 0, exactly the split both other GPUs read. Every design is 585 target plus 100 designed residues at seed 7. Peak 32707 MiB of 81920, no memory pressure. At batch 8 it amortises to 24.775 s per design, 1.79x.

amzn-10q.label: Amazon, Form 10-Q, useful life of servers
amzn-10q.detail: From 1 January 2025 Amazon depreciates a subset of its servers and networking equipment over five years, down from six, citing the pace of AI hardware development. This page's four-year window is one year shorter than that.

caveats: Rows are not a cross-model ranking. Boltz-2 and OpenFold3 do 3 recycles where ESMFold2, Protenix-v2 and OpenDDE do 10, because that is what each ships. Compare a model to itself across hardware.
Accuracy is not compared here. Each stack ran its own settings and every run was checked against its own plDDT, but these numbers are wall-clock and cost.

The A100 ran the same seven cells on the same fixtures. Its host is an AMD EPYC 7513 where the H200 and B200 boxes were Intel Xeon, which matters for the dispatch-bound trunks and is not corrected for.
